title: RTT Resonance Truth Regime
description: Schema for an operational Regime used by the RTT Resonance Truth Service v0.1 model. A Regime defines the bounded conditions, requirements, policies, and permitted responses under which a Claim is evaluated. Regime participates directly in qualification but must remain distinct from dynamic Evidence and the resulting Truth State.

domain.description: Operational domain in which this Regime applies. This remains extensible and is not restricted to the ten canonical Truth Classes.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the operating conditions represented by this Regime.

truth_classes.description: Truth Classes explicitly governed or constrained by this Regime.

observer_context.description: Optional bounded description of the observer, consumer, relying party, or local evaluation perspective for which this Regime applies. Dynamic observational Evidence should remain outside this field.

precision_requirement.description: Optional precision or tolerance requirement for domains where a meaningful quantitative boundary exists.

maximum_age_seconds.description: Optional maximum Evidence age permitted by this Regime, in seconds. Null is appropriate when freshness is not expressed as wall-clock age.

minimum_independent_sources.description: Optional minimum number of structurally independent Sources required by this Regime. Independence must not be inferred from Source count alone.

consequence.description: Optional consequence classification used by the Regime to constrain acceptance or downstream action.

permitted_truth_statuses.description: Truth-State qualification statuses permitted for operational use within this Regime. Presence in this list does not cause an Evaluation to receive that status.

correction_modes.description: Correction modes permitted by this Regime. Actual Correction remains downstream of Evaluation and Truth-State synthesis.

policies.description: Structured governing rules or constraints that participate in Evaluation under this Regime.

required_anchor_ids.description: Optional v0.1 Anchor identifiers explicitly required or recognized by this Regime.

valid_from.description: Optional beginning of the Regime's validity interval.

valid_until.description: Optional end of the Regime's validity interval.

policy_version.description: Optional version or generation of the governing policy or Regime definition.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the Regime definition.

supersedes_regime_id.description: Optional identifier of an earlier Regime superseded by this Regime.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which the Regime record was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent Regime-record update.

metadata.description: Optional domain-specific or implementation metadata. Metadata must not override canonical Regime fields or be used to smuggle dynamic Evidence into the governing boundary.

unit.description: Unit associated with the numeric boundary.

comparison.description: Semantic interpretation of the numeric requirement.

observer_id.description: Optional identifier of the observer, consumer, relying party, or evaluation perspective.

role.description: Optional role performed by the observer within this Regime.

scope.description: Optional bounded scope in which the observer context applies.

policy_id.description: Stable identifier for this governing rule within the Regime.

description.description: Human-readable description of the governing rule.

value.description: Optional domain-native value associated with the rule.

unit.description: Optional unit associated with a numeric rule value.

enforcement.description: Whether the rule is mandatory, advisory, or interpreted according to domain semantics.

examples.name: Low-consequence display clock
examples.description: Temporal Regime permitting bounded Drift for a human-readable display clock while requiring sufficiently coherent independent temporal Evidence.

policies.description: Synthesized temporal Drift must remain within the declared display-clock precision requirement for ordinary operational acceptance.

examples.name: High-consequence temporal evaluation
examples.description: Example Regime demonstrating a stricter temporal boundary without changing the underlying Evidence.
